title: Braid--fluid correspondence: from categorical braiding to vortex dynamics
html:
The categorical braid-group action possesses a direct hydrodynamic interpretation on the brane fluid.

Arnold's geodesic framework. Arnold demonstrated that the Euler equation on (M, g) behaves exactly as the geodesic equation over \mathrm{SDiff}(M) acting under the L^2 metric: \nabla_{\dot\phi}\dot\phi = 0. The velocity vector v = \dot\phi \circ \phi^{-1} solves \partial_t v + \nabla_v v = -\nabla p.

q-deformed diffeomorphisms. The state bundle promotes the classical \mathrm{SDiff}(M) group to \mathrm{SDiff}_q(\mathcal{S}). This imposes two structural shifts:

  1. The L^2 metric upgrades to the Tanaka–Webster inner product. The resulting geodesics solve the quantum Euler equation subject to pressure Q_q.
  2. Confining the state space to flows exhibiting concentrated vorticity across n filaments forces a strict topological quotient onto B_n. The fundamental group of the configuration space \mathrm{Conf}_n(M)/S_n resolves uniquely to B_n.

Braid generators as vortex exchanges. The Artin generator \sigma_i dictates the half-twist spatial exchange of filaments i and i+1. The representation \rho_n(\sigma_i) = \mathrm{id}^{\otimes(i-1)} \otimes c_{V,V} \otimes \mathrm{id}^{\otimes(n-i-1)} (7.2.1) manifests physically as the \mathrm{SU}(2) holonomy traversing the exchange path. The Yang--Baxter equation enforces Reidemeister III, ensuring three-vortex braiding stays rigorously path-independent.

Hecke relation as scattering. The quadratic rule (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0 restricts two-vortex interactions to exactly two terminal eigenvalues: q (symmetric unperturbed pass-through) and -q^{-1} (antisymmetric core reconnection). The universal intensity ratio

  \frac{\text{reconnection}}{\text{pass-through}}
  = q^{-2}

relies entirely on the substrate parameter. This ratio establishes the fluid-dynamical source mechanism for the skein crossing asymmetry.

Helicity as Markov trace. The Jones polynomial J_L(q) operates as the topological helicity governing the vortex tangle. This categorical metric refines classical helicity H = \int v \cdot \omega \, dV, distinguishing topological states invisible to H (separating the trefoil from the unknot). It is evaluated on the closed tangle: each vortex strand is closed by a return arc that adds no crossing, and the closure is a trace on the braid algebra, so it cannot see conjugation (closure).
